text:
sanjay: Heads-up — proposal to add a first-class fallback_policy to all client SDKs so apps can declare how to degrade when their preferred routing target is unavailable. Goal: make platform rollouts + console UX simpler and avoid app-side hacks.

amanda: short version — what shapes does the API take? enum? callback?

sanjay: enum on the wire, plumbed into SDK config. naive sketch: 
```json
{
  "fallback_policy": "regional|cost_preference|none",
  "regional_priority": ["us-west-2", "us-east-1"]
}
```
SDKs would map this to header(s) and local client behavior (fast fail vs queued retry).

ben: two concerns: 1) backward compat for older SDKs/servers, 2) telemetry — we need to see when fallbacks happen (and why).

ciara: +1 on telemetry. We should emit a short telemetry header like `X-RI-Fallback` with values `none|regional|cost_pref` and also an event to the console when fallback happens so customers can see drift.

amanda: how does this interact with model variants + canary rollouts? If a canary is behind and we fallback to main, do we surface that as a rollback or just normal fallback? UX question for console.

sanjay: plan: treat fallback as an orthogonal signal. Console will show fallback counts per route/model version. For canary run we show two metrics: attempted_target_rate vs served_fallback_rate. That helps decide whether canary is starving traffic.

ben: for SDK compat, I'd prefer opt-in. Default behavior should remain unchanged. Introduce header `X-RI-Fallback-OptIn: 1` for SDKs defaulting to new enum. Server ignores missing header, preserving older clients.

ciara: agreed. For telemetry, we should record (a) fallback reason (capacity|error|latency) and (b) final target served. Small JSON payload to our telemetry pipeline is fine. We already have tracing hooks to tie to request_id.

amanda: does anyone object to making the enum extensible on the wire (string values) so we can add new strategies later without breaking? e.g., `cost_threshold:v2` etc.

sanjay: no objection. We'll version the header when semantics change. Backwards-compat: server treats unknown strings as `none` unless `X-RI-Fallback-OptIn` present.

ben: testing plan: add unit tests to SDKs mapping config->headers, e2e sim in staging that forces capacity exhaustion to validate fallback path and console meter. Also add a deprecation notice in release notes for apps that relied on old nonstandard env vars.

ciara: console UX: add a per-route toggle to enable server-side enforcement of fallback policy (so customers can force platform to honor client preference) vs client-only advisory. Default: advisory. Need copy + help text. I'll mock a quick panel.

amanda: release cadence idea: feature-flag rollout across SDKs. Start with Python + TS opt-in beta (minor releases), gather metrics for 2 weeks, then default-on for new major SDK versions.

sanjay: ok owners: eng-platform to implement header handling + server telemetry (ben), SDK leads to add config + header (amanda & ben), console to add UI + metrics (ciara). I'll open RFC doc and link PRs.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: routing-service/staging -> 2026-04-02T18:00Z (will include header parsing + telemetry schema changes).

amanda: thanks — I'll start the Python patch and include opt-in env var `RI_FALLBACK_OPTIN=1` for quick testing.

ben: small nit: call the header `X-RI-Fallback-Policy` (explicit). Also add `X-RI-Fallback-Reason` when server chooses fallback.

ciara: adding to console telemetry backlog now. I put a link to the mock in the RFC.

sanjay: perfect — let's keep the initial SDK surface minimal: one config key, one opt-in header, one telemetry header. We can iterate after metrics. :thumbsup:
